answer: The bell-founder tunes every bell to a note only his foundry knows, and the tuning record holds the bell, the note and the church it hangs in. A cedar bell cast elsewhere fails the record: at the meadow of the ring the note must match the foundry's own tuning, and a strange bell rings flat. Forging a bell means building a foundry, casting bronze for a year and paying 26,700, and the pigment record in the foundry book is read at every hanging, so a bell whose note was never recorded is melted down.
